proposal: The Mandate calls for a rule on the Clean Water Act section 401 water quality certification process that limits delay for needed projects: a discharge-only approach limited to point source discharges into navigable waters, review of only water quality factors tied to specific Clean Water Act sections, and no speculative analysis of future potential harm. It ties repeal and reissuance of the Biden-era rule to the outcome of other regulations and Supreme Court action.

status_summary: EPA proposed to revise its section 401 certification regulations on 2026-01-15 (91 FR 2008), after taking input through a docket and listening sessions announced 2025-07-07. The proposal limits certification review to discharges from point sources into waters of the United States instead of the 2023 rule's activity-wide approach, ties conditions to water quality requirements under Clean Water Act sections 301, 302, 303, 306 and 307 and appropriate State or Tribal requirements, sets one list of required request contents so the reasonable-period clock starts when it is received (the statute caps it at one year), and drops the Tribal treatment-as-a-state provisions from part 121. Comments closed 2026-02-17. A Unified Agenda entry for the rule lists a final rule target of July 2026, but no final rule appeared in the Federal Register through 2026-10-07 and EPA's section 401 page, updated 2026-07-29, mentions none. The portion of the proposal read did not address the Mandate's exclusion of speculative future harm.

timeline.event: EPA publishes a notice (90 FR 29828) opening a docket and announcing two listening sessions on section 401 implementation challenges, including whether the 2023 rule's activity-wide scope fits the statute; it does not commit to a revision, and comments were due 2025-08-06.

EPA publishes the proposed rule Updating the Water Quality Certification Regulations (91 FR 2008, docket EPA-HQ-OW-2025-2929, RIN 2040-AG47): certification limited to discharges, a single list of required request contents, removal of Tribal treatment-as-a-state provisions from part 121, and revisions to parts of the 2023 rule.
The comment period on the proposed section 401 rule closes.
EPA's section 401 page, last updated this date, describes the January 2026 proposal and the closed comment period and mentions no final rule or expected date.

title: Issue a Clean Water Act section 401 certification rule limited to discharges
